attempts.plan:
1. Read the two input files into pandas DataFrames:  
   • “borough_no2.csv” – columns: borough, avg_no2_value  
   • “neighbours.csv” – columns: borough, neighbour (one row per pair)  
   (If they are combined differently, adapt the column names but keep the same idea.)

2. Handle missing values up-front.  
   • Keep every row whose avg_no2_value is not NaN; drop the 4 rows whose value is missing.  
   • Store the list of the dropped boroughs so we never classify them later.  
   • In all later calculations, any reference to a missing-value borough contributes 0 to the weight matrix and 0 to the sums (i.e. it is ignored rather than treated as a zero reading).

3. Build a symmetric binary spatial-weight matrix W (n × n, where n = number of non-missing boroughs).  
   • w_ij = 1 if borough j is borough i itself or appears in i’s neighbour list AND both i and j have non-missing values; otherwise 0.  
   • Pre-compute for each i: S_i = Σ_j w_ij  (the number of members in the local “i + neighbours” area).

4. Compute the global mean and standard deviation of NO₂ among the n non-missing boroughs:  
      X̄  = (Σ x_i) / n  
      S   = sqrt[ Σ(x_i – X̄)² / (n–1) ]

5. For every borough i that retained a value, calculate the Getis-Ord Gi* z-score:  
      Gi*₍i₎ = [ Σ_j w_ij x_j  – X̄ · S_i ]  
               -------------------------------------------------------------  
               S · sqrt[ (n·Σ_j w_ij² – S_i²) / (n–1) ]  
   (With a binary W, Σ_j w_ij² = S_i because every non-zero w_ij = 1.)

6. Decision rule for significance (two-tailed):  
   • If Gi*₍i₎ >  2.576  → HOT spot at 99 %  
   • If Gi*₍i₎ >  1.960  → HOT spot at 95 %  
   • If Gi*₍i₎ < –2.576 → COLD spot at 99 %  
   • If Gi*₍i₎ < –1.960 → COLD spot at 95 %  
   • Otherwise not significant.  
   (You may keep track of the confidence level but only the HOT/COLD label and the actual Gi* value are printed.)

7. Build a list like   
   results = [f"{borough} (HOT, Gi*={gi_val:.3f})", …]  
   for every borough whose Gi* meets the chosen threshold, skipping any borough that originally had a missing NO₂ value.

8. Print exactly two lines:  
   • data_points_used = n          (the count after removing the 4 NaNs)  
   • FINAL ANSWER: …              (join the strings in ‘results’ with “, ”; if ‘results’ is empty print “FINAL ANSWER: none”).

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# ---------- 1. Load data ----------
NO2_PATH = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_no2_Q4_2021.csv"
ADJ_PATH = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

no2_df = pd.read_csv(NO2_PATH)           # columns: borough, avg_no2_value
adj_df = pd.read_csv(ADJ_PATH)           # columns: borough, neighbor

# ---------- 2. Drop boroughs with missing NO2 ----------
valid_no2_df = no2_df.dropna(subset=["avg_no2_value"]).reset_index(drop=True)
valid_boroughs = set(valid_no2_df["borough"])

# keep original index for later mapping
valid_no2_df = valid_no2_df.set_index("borough")

# number of data points actually used
n = len(valid_no2_df)

# ---------- 3. Build symmetric binary weight matrix W ----------
# Start with adjacency list, keep only pairs where both boroughs have data
adj_pairs = adj_df[adj_df["borough"].isin(valid_boroughs) & adj_df["neighbor"].isin(valid_boroughs)]

# Add the reversed direction to make it symmetric
reversed_pairs = adj_pairs.rename(columns={"borough": "neighbor", "neighbor": "borough"})
sym_adj = pd.concat([adj_pairs, reversed_pairs]).drop_duplicates()

# Each borough is also its own neighbor (include self-weight)
self_pairs = pd.DataFrame({
    "borough": list(valid_boroughs),
    "neighbor": list(valid_boroughs)
})

sym_adj = pd.concat([sym_adj, self_pairs]).drop_duplicates()

# Create mapping from name to positional index
idx_map = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(valid_no2_df.index)}
W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=int)
for _, row in sym_adj.iterrows():
    i = idx_map[row["borough"]]
    j = idx_map[row["neighbor"]]
    W[i, j] = 1

# ---------- 4. Pre-compute statistics ----------
X = valid_no2_df["avg_no2_value"].values
X_bar = X.mean()
S = X.std(ddof=1)           # sample std (n-1 in denom)

# Pre-compute row sums and sq row sums
S_i = W.sum(axis=1)                 # number of members in local area (incl. itself)
# With binary weights, sum of squares over j is the same as S_i
sum_wij_sq = S_i

# ---------- 5. Compute Gi* for every borough ----------
Gi_star = []
for i in range(n):
    sum_wij_xj = (W[i] * X).sum()
    numerator = sum_wij_xj - X_bar * S_i[i]
    denominator = S * np.sqrt((n * sum_wij_sq[i] - S_i[i] ** 2) / (n - 1))
    Gi_star.append(numerator / denominator if denominator != 0 else np.nan)

Gi_star = np.array(Gi_star)

# ---------- 6. Determine significant hot/cold spots ----------
results = []
for i, z in enumerate(Gi_star):
    borough = valid_no2_df.index[i]
    if abs(z) > 1.96:        # 95% two-tailed threshold
        label = "HOT" if z > 0 else "COLD"
        results.append(f"{borough} ({label}, Gi*={z:.3f})")

# ---------- 7. Print required output ----------
print(f"data_points_used = {n}")
if results:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
